preview: An on-campus interview experience for a 2023 FTE role at BNY Mellon, detailing the online assessment, company presentation, two technical rounds, and an HR round.
content: Software Developer Interview Experience Dushant Harinkhede| B.Tech Computer Engineering 2020-24 For 2023 FTE (On-campus) Eligibility: 7.5+ CGPA Round 1 - Online Assessment ( August 10, 2023) Online Test conducted on Hackerrank Platform having 4 DSA Questions to be completed within 90 Minutes. 1. Easy (50 Marks) Count User Logins - On reading this question it seemed to be quite easy but then I thought I should start with the last question and will come to it in the end but didn’t get enough time to attempt this in the end. 2. Medium I (75 Marks) - Can’t recall the question but I was able to solve this completely. 3. Medium II (75 Marks) Server Investment - We were given with the arrays num_servers,money,upgrade and sell ,each with n integers.We had to determine the maximum number of servers that can be upgraded to ensure optimal network security. I was able to solve this question completely and it was easy though. 4. Hard (100 Marks) Team Formation - Given a list of employees, where each is assigned a numeric score, and there are certain rules for finding the sum of scores of selected employees. Rules - 1. The employee with the highest score among the first k employees or the last k employees in the score list is selected. 2. Selected Employees are removed from the score list. 3. The process continues until team_size is achieved. Example - score[] = [10, 20, 10, 15, 5, 30, 20] team_size = 2 k = 3 Initially, we select first k i.e [10, 20, 10] or last k [5, 30, 20] so, 30 is selected and removed from the list. Second time, we have first k i.e [10,20,10] or last k [15,5,20] we take 20 and remove it. Thus our team reaches a size of team_size so we stop and return 30 + 20 = 50. I was able to solve this completely using the priority queue. First only 19 students were shortlisted but 1 day prior to the interview 3 of the 19 got placed in some other dream company so on the day of interview 8 more candidates were shortlisted hence the total came to 24 candidates for interview. Round 2 - PPT talk about BNY ( August 17, 2023) Many of you will not consider it as a round but I will say it is one of the most important rounds to collect points to say in the HR round. Like I made note of some points which they said in ppt such as : 1) 1/3rd of world's total money goes through BNY daily 2) BNY work on all the tech stack may it be old or new. They work on java Springboot to React and AI/ML. 3) BNY the world's largest custodian bank. So these were all the points which I used in the HR interview Round to make them feel that their presentation was worth it and I was paying attention to that. Round 3 - Technical Interview-1(45-50 mins) It was an offline interview in the college itself on the same day of ppt. The interview began with an introduction after that she asked what courses have you studied. I told her that I know OOPS,DBMS,SQL,OS and DSA. (always remember tell the interviewer that courses only in which u are confident enough to answer) Then she started with OOPS where she asked me questions : 1) Explain abstraction with real life example 2) Write code for abstraction So to this i explained everything about abstraction, abstract classes,pure virtual function and how pure virtual function is helping in abstraction. 3) Then she made me changes in the code and asked to predict the output One of which I remember which I was not able to answer was like she asked me what will happen if we pass the object of child class to parent class in abstraction. After the interview I searched about this and I found it was related to object slicing. 4) What is inheritance and types of inheritance and Write code for all the types After this she moved on to DSA part : 1) Implement linked list - Here I just explained how we will create a linked list. She was satisfied so she didn't ask me to code. 2) Find the frequency of maximum occurring element in linked list - Here she asked me to write code so I solved it using maps. 3) Tell me the data structure which could search element in o(1) time - maps 4) Which DS could be implemented for sql databases - it was an application based question for maps 5) Then she asked me to explain merge sort and explain time complexity mathematically. - So I explained this by creating a recursion tree as she said not to explain using code. After this she asked me one puzzle and a sql query. Puzzle was quite popular one : https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-1-how-to-measure-45-minutes-using-two-identical-wires/ - Since I was familiar with this puzzle I was able to explain this well using pen and paper. And the sql query was like there were 2 tables emp and emp details. Find the employees whose salaries are greater than 20000. With this the 1st round was over and I thought I wasn’t up to the mark in this round and I would not be shortlisted for round 2.But after 2 hrs the result came and I was called for round 2 so I can say that she must have liked my explanation.After tech round 1, 6 students were eliminated so there were 18 students for round 2 tech interview. Round 4 - Technical Interview-2 (40 mins) This interview round also started with the introduction where first the interviewer introduced himself and then he asked me to introduce. One thing to note here was while introducing himself he said currently he is working on backend technologies from the past 6-7 years. So in my introduction part where I used to tell interviewers that I am CTO of Rangawardhan where we built the site for the committee to take registration of events. I cleared the interviewer in the introduction itself that we haven’t implemented backend so that he could not go deep in backend questions. Note : If you have been part of any committee technical team, do mention it in your introduction. Sometimes interviewers can visit that website and ask questions on it. Then he asked me if I knew OOPS. I said yes then he asked me these questions : 1) What are SOLID principles and Some jargon terms in OOPS to which I was not familiar . - After listening to these terms I was like “ bhai yeh kya puchrahe ho sunn hi mai pehli baar rhaa(in my mind)”. I had little knowledge of solid principles but I said this was not part of our academics so I don't have any idea about all this. 2) Inheritance with code and real life example Here I explained everything about inheritance in detail with code how we can inherit classes publicly and privately. What will happen to private,public and protected data members when inherited publicly,privately and protected mode.Then he asked me to change the written code for runtime polymorphism.So I did that then he asked me to predict output after some changes in code 3) Explain Early binding and late binding It simply means compile and runtime polymorphism so I explained this with code. Then he asked if you know about sorting algos. I said yes and then named all so he asked me to explain the step by step working of insertion sort and write code of it and then do a dry run of code.So I first explained the algorithm by taking an example and solved it step by step and then i wrote code for it adding to it he also asked me for writing code for swap function so I wrote the swap function by both the methods using 3rd variable and w/o using 3rd variable. So this round was quite good and simple and the interviewer seemed to be happy. Then after 10 mins I was called for the HR round.After tech round 2, 4 students were eliminated so there were 14 students for HR interview. Round 5 - HR Round (15-20 mins) In this round first he asked how was your day and interview, then he had feedback of me from both the rounds so he asked me why you have average feedback for oops concept.I was shocked but instead of opposing it I said it might be due to the reason that it was the course in our 2nd year and from past 5-6 months I am not in touch with oops and he was fine with the answer. Then he started with the most expected question : 1) Why do you want to join bny ? - Answering to this question i used the points which i collected during ppt round 2) what do you mean by growth(it was referring to growth in career)? - I said it is like a ladder which provides a path to success and then explained it further by aligning it with my future goals and how bny could help me to achieve it. 3) What are the different committees you were part of? - I told him about each and every role and work that I did. 4) Why did you were part of these many number of committees ?(as i was part of 4-5 college committees) - I was able to give a satisfactory answer to HR. 5) As i was CTO and said we built the site for the committee so he visited the site and liked it so asked which tech stack you used? And why you used ReactJS? 6) What is your family background? 7) Since I was interned at UBS he asked me what would you choose if you get offer from both and why ? This round of interview was very chill and at the concluding part of the interview the HR said we had very good conversation, hope we will meet soon.So after listening to these words I was pretty confident that I could be selected. After waiting for around 2-3 hrs after my interview they released the results and happily I was one of those 12 students who were selected for the SDE role at BNY. Tips : DBMS and SQL: 1) If you don't have any knowledge of DBMS then you can start with the knowledge gate youtube channel or gate smashers. Both are good. Personally, I preferred knowledge gate. 2) You should have gone through all the interview questions of interviewbit. https://www.interviewbit.com/dbms-interview-questions/ 3) For sql if you are at a very beginner level you can learn sql through gate smashers or w3school, both are good resources to start with. 4) Now after some hands-on basic sql you can watch this playlist from techftq youtube channel. It has a good playlist of 7 videos related to interview questions. https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLavw5C92dz9HQQ_COgGb7kf_1H8UWUBxO 5) For practicing SQL queries everyone will suggest practicing on hacker rank or leetcode but I personally liked this site for SQL practice. https://platform.stratascratch.com/coding?code_type=1 6) Now for me these two blogs were really helpful for SQL interviews.If you have less time to prepare, like 1 month or so then you can prepare from these two websites.(but you should have basic knowledge of SQL) https://www.edureka.co/blog/interview-questions/sql-query-interview-questions#fetchaddressname →Mostly Covers all important sql query questions https://techtfq.com/blog/top-20-sql-interview-questions →top 25 important sql Questions. This much is more than enough for sql and DBMS. OOPS: 1) Since my first language to code was c++ so I did my OOPS in c++ only. 2) One of the best resources to follow for the oops concept for me was code with harry youtube channel. If you have time you should definitely watch the CWH playlist. https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLu0W_9lII9agpFUAlPFe_VNSlXW5uE0YL 3) Try to make your own notes, else if you don’t make you can follow these notes for revision. https://www.linkedin.com/posts/madhavvarjuntthukral-b41564183_oops-ugcPost-7024321442649378816-xmY4/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_android It includes all the important questions which are asked in the interview. 4) Don't just study the concepts, implement them in code as well. You may be asked to demonstrate these concepts in C++ or Java. 5) While preparing concepts of oops like inheritance, polymorphism, etc you should have the ability to explain these concepts with real-life examples. It shows that you can implement your study in the real world. OS : 1) It was the only subject which was least asked to me in my interviews out of 6 company interviews. It was asked in only one and that's also DE Shaw. 2) So from my personal experience don't give much time on this subject just watch gate smashers OS the playlist and make notes and go through interview bit interview questions. DSA: For Binary Search, Stacks, Sliding Window (MUST), Heap - Aditya Verma. For DP, Trees, and Graphs - take U forward. 1) Always revise the sorting algorithms, basic data structure questions because they are frequently asked in interviews such as quick sort, merge sort, stack using a queue, queue using stack, graph traversals, etc. 2) Make notes for each topic that you cover. These could be on some pattern that you identified in such questions as finding Kth order statistics in an array being related to a heap or some syntax that you find tough to remember such as the declaration of the priority queue in C++. 3) Don't hit a trial by submitting your code; it just wastes time. Rather do a dry run of example input and expected output. You won't be asking an interviewer to confirm your code multiple times. so develop the habit of verifying it twice and submitting it once. 4) Sometimes you may be asked to write the driver code, and data structure implementation along with the algorithm for the given question - in both online tests and interviews. Do practice writing driver code for a linked list,tree, and graph questions. (all these tips of DSA I took it from Pankaj kushlani(our senior) interview experience as all these tips are really good to follow )
